setup.zh: 娘把最后一点白面烙成两张饼，厚的给你；爹拿麻布缠紧了膝盖。娘说：打得过就打，打不过就跑。
setup.en: Mother bakes the last of the white flour into two flatbreads, the thick one for you; Father binds his knee tight. Mother says: fight if you can win; if not, run.

recap.zh: 娘把最后一点白面烙成饼塞给你：「打不过就跑——跑不丢人。」
recap.en: Mother gave you bread from the last of the flour: "If you can't win, run — there's no shame in running."

zh: 灶间亮了灯。最后一点白面，烙成两张饼。
en: A lamp in the kitchen. The last of the flour, baked into two breads.

story.zh:
你关上窗，一回身，灶间的灯已经亮了。

你娘蹲在灶前烙饼。

白面的。

你家那个装白面的小布袋，你知道，已经瘪了一个月了，瘪得跟你爹的钱袋一样——你爹的钱袋，你从来没见它鼓过，你一度怀疑它生下来就是瘪的。你娘把最后一点面全抖了出来，抖了三遍，连布袋缝里的面粉都拍了出来，烙了两张饼。

一张厚。一张薄。

你爹坐在炕沿上，拿一块旧麻布，一圈一圈地缠他的左膝。缠完了，他站起来，试着走了两步。脸上的肉抽了一下，又若无其事地坐了回去，冲你咧嘴一笑：

**爹**：没事。老毛病。它今天话有点多。

**娘**：（没回头）他爹。真去黑松岭？

**爹**：前山空了。

**娘**：你那腿——

**爹**：腿不行。（顿了顿）还有孩子的腿。

你娘手里的铲子，停了一下。

然后她把那张厚的饼铲了出来，拿一块干净的布包好，走过来，塞进你怀里。

薄的那张，她给了你爹。

她自己一张都没有。

你娘蹲下来，看着你的眼睛。她的声音很低，低得只有你们两个人听得见。

**娘**：你爹老实。一辈子不会算计人，也不会防着人。你不一样。你随我。

她伸手，掐掉了你衣襟上的一根线头。

**娘**：山里的东西，比马三还狠。遇事，先想，再动。想明白了，打得过就打，打不过就跑。跑，不丢人。

**你**：嗯。

**娘**：还有。（顿了顿）昨天那一下，娘看见了。

你抬起头。

**娘**：你没还手。对的。

**娘**：你回的那句嘴——（她的嘴角，极轻极轻地，动了一下）也对。

她把你额前的头发，拢了拢。

**娘**：可也别忘了。

你爹在身后咳了两声，背起了那张弓。

你娘站在门口——门口没有门，门还在{伴}家的菜地里——看着你们一大一小两个背影，走进天边那一线灰白里。

她没有喊。也没有挥手。

她就那么一直站着。站到你回头，也看不见她了。
story.en:
You close the window and turn round; the kitchen lamp is already lit.

Your mother is crouched at the stove, making flatbread.

White flour.

The little cloth bag your family keeps the white flour in, you know, has been flat for a month — as flat as your father's purse. (Your father's purse: you have never once seen it full, and for a while you suspected it was born flat.) Your mother has shaken out every last bit of flour, shaken it three times, patted out even what was caught in the seams, and made two flatbreads.

One thick. One thin.

Your father sits on the edge of the brick bed, winding an old strip of hemp round his left knee, turn after turn. Done, he stands and tries two steps. The muscles of his face twitch; he sits back down as if nothing happened and grins at you:

**Father:** It's fine. Old trouble. It's a bit chatty today.

**Mother:** (without turning round) Husband. You're really going to Black Pine Ridge?

**Father:** The front slopes are empty.

**Mother:** That leg of yours —

**Father:** The leg's no good. (a pause) The child's legs are.

The spatula in your mother's hand stops for a moment.

Then she lifts the thick flatbread out, wraps it in a clean cloth, comes over and tucks it inside your jacket.

The thin one she gives your father.

She keeps none for herself.

Your mother crouches down and looks you in the eye. Her voice is low, so low only the two of you can hear it.

**Mother:** Your father's honest. All his life he's never schemed against anyone, and never guarded against anyone either. You're different. You take after me.

She reaches out and pinches a loose thread off your collar.

**Mother:** The things in the mountain are crueller than Ma San. When something happens, think first, then move. Once you've thought it through: if you can win, fight. If you can't, run. Running's no shame.

**You:** Mm.

**Mother:** And. (a pause) Yesterday. I saw.

You look up.

**Mother:** You didn't hit back. That was right.

**Mother:** The thing you said back to him — (the corner of her mouth moves, very, very slightly) — that was right too.

She smooths the hair off your forehead.

**Mother:** But don't forget it, either.

Behind you your father coughs twice and shoulders the bow.

Your mother stands in the doorway — there's no door in the doorway; the door is still in {伴}'s family's vegetable patch — watching the two of you, one big and one small, walk into the thin grey line at the edge of the sky.

She doesn't call out. She doesn't wave.

She just stands there, and keeps standing, until you look back and can't see her anymore.

exits.means: sets off with father into the mountain, moves on
